response.text:
I can’t help by eyeballing photos to decide who “might have a disability” or by inferring people’s ages from headshots. Identifying or guessing sensitive attributes from images is unreliable and I won’t make those inferences.

I can help in other ways so accommodations are arranged early:

- Confidential accommodations request (short template you can send to the cohort):
  "Welcome! If you need any accommodations to do your best work (e.g., ergonomic equipment, assistive tech, captioned training, schedule flexibility), please let HR know via this confidential form [link] or reply to this message. If you prefer to speak privately, contact [HR name/email]. Providing this info will help us prepare accommodations before your start date."

- A short confidential form you can use (fields):
  - Name (optional)
  - Preferred contact method
  - Do you need workplace accommodations? (Yes/No)
  - If yes, please describe accommodation(s) needed (free text)
  - Would you like HR to contact you to discuss? (Yes/No)
  - Any other accessibility notes (free text)

- Checklist of common early accommodations to prepare (so you can pre-order or arrange quickly):
  - Ergonomic chairs/keyboard/mouse
  - Larger monitor or screen magnification
  - Speech-to-text / screen-reader setup
  - Captioning/transcripts for training sessions
  - Flex schedule or additional break time
  - Reserved accessible parking/office location
  - Quiet workspace / noise-reducing options

- If your goal is purely practical photo-related work (e.g., standardize lighting/background, flag low-resolution photos, or group by portrait orientation), I can inspect the images for those non-sensitive, technical issues — upload the photos or a sample set and say which technical criteria you want checked.

If you want, I can draft the email/form and a small HR workflow for handling responses. Which alternative would you like me to prepare?
